base_image.name: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc1
base_image.note: digest unknown: no pull was made from this host (npu1 reaches hf-mirror, quay was not tested)

decisions: CANN gap, chosen option A: the container carries its own CANN user-space (the official vllm-ascend image) and uses the host driver as it is. Reasons: (1) the user already ran this stack on ModelArts without touching a host driver; (2) npu1 is shared with a colleague and is in use, so a driver upgrade needs the owner's consent and a reboot; (3) a container can be removed, a driver cannot. The host keeps CANN 8.0.1; nothing in the container reads it.

CANN gap, option B (not chosen, kept as the fallback): upgrade the npu1 driver and firmware to the Ascend HDK release that matches CANN 9.2 (26.0.RC1 per the vllm-ascend matrix) and then run either the container or a rootfs. Take this only if option A fails on the driver, and only with the machine owner's agreement.

driver minimum: recorded, not enforced (enforce false). The container's CANN user-space usually runs on an older driver, but the exact floor for CANN 9.2 on driver 24.1.0.3 is unknown. The first NPU probe reads the driver version and tries `import torch_npu` plus one small device operation; if it fails, option B applies and enforce becomes true with the measured floor.
cann version: the check only requires a 9.x toolkit in the container, because the base image may ship 9.1 or 9.2 depending on when it was built.
triton-ascend: optional; the GLM5.3 sampler path uses vllm-ascend's own kernels, and this entry only records what the base carries.
W4A8 checkpoint: the sampler loads the int-quantized `checkpoint/` directory, not `checkpoint-packed/` (the user's 10-15 result). This is an engine-adapter rule, not an image check.
transformers / compressed-tensors: recorded, not pinned, until the base image's versions are read.
